com.vector.cfg.dom.runtimesys.groovy.api

Interface ISelectedCommunicationElements


  • @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
public interface ISelectedCommunicationElements
    ISelectedCommunicationElements represents a selection of ICommunicationElements and provides further actions on it. The selection can contain both complex (e.g. a record) as well as also simple communication elements.

    • Method Detail

      • assureMappedTo

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.List<IDataMapping> assureMappedTo(@Nonnull
                                                              java.util.List<IAbstractSignalInstance> abstractSignalInstances)

        assureMappedTo(List) does the same as mapTo(List) but ignores communication element and abstract signal instance pairs for which a data mapping does already exist.

        If you want to create complex mappings (currently only SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings) the given abstractSignalInstances should contain the group signals right after the parent signal group instances.
        For a client server to signal mapping, select call and return signal instance directly after each other.

        Parameters:
        abstractSignalInstances - The IAbstractSignalInstances to be mapped to the communication elements. The order is relevant, the communication elements will be matched to the abstract signal instances via index.
        Returns:
        The newly created IDataMappings mapping communication element and abstract signal instance pairs which were not mapped to each other. Mappings are returned expanded, so the returned list contains also leaf data mappings.
        Throws:
        SelectionException - When creating one of the data mappings is not possible, a similar mapping does already exist or there is something wrong with the order. See Automation Interface simple API documentation for more details about the checks.

      • mapTo

        @PublishedMethod
java.util.List<IDataMapping> mapTo(@Nonnull
                                                     java.util.List<IAbstractSignalInstance> abstractSignalInstances)

        mapTo(List) maps the ICommunicationElements which are represented by this ISelectedCommunicationElements to the given IAbstractSignalInstances via index matching. So the first communication element will be mapped to the first abstract signal instance, the second to the second abstract signal instance and so on.
        In case you want to ignore communication element and system signal pairs for which a mapping does already exist please use assureMappedTo(List).
        If you want to map your communication elements to system signals using name matching please use IRuntimeSystemApi.selectCommunicationElements(groovy.lang.Closure).

        If you want to create complex mappings (currently only SenderReceiverToSignalGroupMappings) the given abstractSignalInstances should contain the group signals right after the parent signal group instances.
        For a client server to signal mapping, select call and return signal instance directly after each other.

        Parameters:
        abstractSignalInstance - The IAbstractSignalInstances to be mapped to the communication elements. The order is relevant, the communication elements will be matched to the abstract signal instances via index.
        Returns:
        The created IDataMappings expanded. That means also the leaf data mappings.
        Throws:
        SelectionException - When creating one of the data mappings is not possible, a similar mapping does already exist or there is something wrong with the order. See Automation Interface simple API documentation for more details about the checks.
